chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: His small band at the Zanzibar and first record
summary: After Redman, Thomas fronts a small band at the Zanzibar, records 'Poor But Happy', loses his piano player Clyde Hart one night, and resents being billed under another name.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: That's right. What about some of the... Where did you go after you left the band, Foots?
Well, what happened, Don... Don was (?) in going to Europe. But I didn't want to go nowhere. So I got busy... My first record came out when I was in the Zanzibar.
And I had another hit! The first record was... What the heck, I ain't never gonna forget that, should never forget it...

No. The first record was "Poor(?) But Happy." And it was a little hit. Because the guys used to come home from the road and say, "Man, you got a hit out there." They'd heard it. It was an instrumental. So I got a chance to take the small band into Zanzibar. And I had already opened my studio teaching. So I had this little band, and I was doing good.

And one night, my piano player don't show -- Clyde Hart. And I didn't have nothin' but a piano and drums; I didn't have no guitar or nothin'. Piano, drums and bass. Because I didn't have about five or six pieces. And he don't show up. And that just killed my band. Because the least he could have done is got somebody... Because he had a recording date. See, Clyde Hart was the first piano player that got away from oom-pah. He was the first one to do that chord thing, you know. And he was very popular in recording. He was a good piano player, too.
And the one thing that's kind of bugged me... I used to... I thought I had a little name going. But the

guy wanted... He could have easily used my name, Walter Thomas... He wanted to call me Hal Thomas or something. And I was advertised...Joe...Joe... What's his name? He had a club on the East Side, too. Joe... I can't think of his name. Anyway, he wanted to change my name. Now, I got the gig with the small band because the guy, the piano player that he was crazy about that he wanted to give a small band to didn't belong to 802, so he couldn't bring a band in. So it left it up to me to bring a small band in there. I got my break from being with Don Redman.
